[operator-attested] Final store state for the scheduling-affecting criterion.

`rebar doctor` against this repository tracker reports 8 findings, all mis-escalated. For each, the BLOCKED side (source for depends_on, target for blocks) is closed:
03a9-e6d1-4acc-435d, 2aa6-726a-ea56-4d6c, 38be-a778-43f5-4a4e, 8d39-85d7-8f34-45e6, 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d, 8784-c2d7-c395-4478 (blocks, so target), e3bd-8cd2-35f1-406b, ea39-c2d1-e26a-4ee6.

A closed blocked-side can never appear in ready or next-batch, so 0 of 8 affect scheduling. Each is blocked from repair by add_dependency correctly refusing a link whose source is closed.

Cumulative: 18 legacy bad edges found, 12 repaired (all 9 ancestor-blocking + 3 mis-escalated), 8 inert residuals. Pre-repair anchor tag written at 962624641cae.

Correction recorded against my own Approach text: I had claimed the redirect record is "kept as the loud signal" so escalation is never silent. That is true only on the CLI path. rebar.link() calls composer.link_core(..., quiet=True) (src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615), and quiet redirects stdout/stderr into a StringIO sink (src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:628), so library and MCP callers have the record DISCARDED. That is the same silence bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 reported, still present on the MCP path — which is how agents actually create links. It predates this story and is unchanged by it; recorded as follow-up on the doctor epics rather than fixed here.
